subject: Copywriting
title: Humor in Copy
description: A 60-second lesson on Humor in Copy.

hook.text: Old Spice's 'The Man Your Man Could Smell Like' is the most shared ad ever. Humor made body wash go viral.

buildup.text: Humor creates positive associations. If an ad makes you laugh, you remember the brand fondly.

discovery.text: Funny ads are shared 3x more than serious ones. Laughter triggers the same reward circuits as food and sex.

twist.text: Humor is risky. A joke that flops becomes cringe. What's funny in one culture offends in another.

climax.text: The best humor serves the message. If you remove the joke and the ad still sells, the humor was decoration.

punchline.text: Funny gets shared. But humor must serve the sale.

quiz.question: How much more are funny ads shared compared to serious ones?

details.summary: Humor lowers defenses, creates likability, and makes messages memorable. Funny ads are shared more, remembered longer, and generate more positive brand associations. But humor is risky — what's hilarious to one audience can offend another.
details.whyItMatters: Humor is one of the highest-reward, highest-risk tools in copywriting. Understanding what makes humor effective — surprise, relatability, and timing — helps writers use it strategically rather than recklessly.
takeaways: Humor increases ad recall by up to 50% compared to serious ads
Self-deprecating humor builds trust by signaling confidence
Humor must be relevant to the product to drive sales, not just entertainment

faq.question: When does humor in copy fail?
faq.answer: When it overshadows the product (people remember the joke but not the brand), when it's culturally insensitive, or when the product is serious (medical, legal, financial). Humor also ages badly — today's joke can become tomorrow's cringe.

faq.question: What type of humor works best in advertising?
faq.answer: Self-deprecating humor, unexpected twists, and observational humor about shared experiences work broadly. Inside jokes build community among niche audiences. The safest humor surprises without punching down and connects back to the product's benefit.
